en_meaning: To lower in rank, prestige, or esteem; to humiliate
vi_meaning: Hạ thấp phẩm giá, làm nhục
example_sentence: Refusing to abase himself before the military tribunal, the dissident author maintained an unyielding posture of moral defiance.

en_meaning: To make someone feel embarrassed, disconcerted, or ashamed
vi_meaning: Làm bối rối, làm ngượng ngùng
example_sentence: Neither the scathing criticism of the press nor the icy reception from parliament could abash the outspoken reformer.

en_meaning: To become less intense, active, or widespread
vi_meaning: Làm dịu đi, thuyên giảm, lắng xuống
example_sentence: Meteorologists cautioned coastal residents that even if the tropical storm's gale-force winds should abate, catastrophic storm surges remained imminent.

en_meaning: To shorten a word, phrase, or text by omitting letters
vi_meaning: Rút ngắn, viết tắt
example_sentence: Constrained by the prohibitive cost per word on transatlantic telegraph cables, foreign correspondents had to abbreviate their battlefield dispatches without sacrificing strategic clarity.

en_meaning: To formally give up a position of power or responsibility
vi_meaning: Thoái vị, từ bỏ quyền lực
example_sentence: Faced with widespread mutiny among the imperial armed forces and the imminent collapse of the capital, the emperor was pressured to abdicate his throne.

en_meaning: The action of forcibly taking someone away against their will
vi_meaning: Sự bắt cóc, chiếm đoạt người trái phép
example_sentence: The clandestine abduction of the reformist senator sparked widespread outrage and ignited weeks of protest outside the presidential palace.

en_meaning: Departing from an accepted standard or normal course
vi_meaning: Lệch lạc, khác thường so với quy chuẩn
example_sentence: Evolutionary biologists discovered that the aberrant migratory behavior of the alpine finches was a direct phenotypic response to unseasonably warm winters.

en_meaning: To encourage or assist someone to do something wrong
vi_meaning: Tiếp tay, xúi giục làm điều xấu
example_sentence: The forensic audit revealed that regional bank directors had conspired to abet the fraudulent venture by falsifying liquidity disclosures.

en_meaning: A state of temporary disuse or suspension
vi_meaning: Tình trạng tạm hoãn, đình chỉ
example_sentence: With the outbreak of the civil war, construction on the transcontinental railway fell into abeyance until federal funding could be restored.

en_meaning: To regard with disgust and hatred
vi_meaning: Ghê tởm, căm ghét tột độ
example_sentence: Enlightenment philosophers such as Voltaire came to abhor religious persecution, advocating instead for universal toleration and civil liberty.

en_meaning: Experienced to a maximum degree or completely without pride or dignity
vi_meaning: Hèn hạ, khốn cùng, cùng cực
example_sentence: Living in abject squalor on the periphery of the industrial boomtown, the displaced miners organized one of the earliest labor unions in the region.

en_meaning: To solemnly renounce a belief, cause, or claim
vi_meaning: Tuyên thệ từ bỏ, khước từ trang trọng
example_sentence: Summoned before the ecclesiastical court, the astronomer refused to abjure his empirical findings regarding the orbital mechanics of planetary bodies.

en_meaning: The act of washing oneself, often used in a religious context
vi_meaning: Lễ tẩy trần, việc tắm rửa thanh tẩy
example_sentence: Archaeological excavations at the temple complex revealed stone conduits designed specifically for the ritual ablution of priests prior to sacrifice.

en_meaning: The act of renouncing or rejecting something; self-denial
vi_meaning: Sự từ bỏ quyền lợi, sự quên mình
example_sentence: The ascetic monk’s life was defined by profound abnegation, renouncing all hereditary wealth and titles to minister to the destitute.

en_meaning: To formally put an end to a system, practice, or institution
vi_meaning: Bãi bỏ, hủy bỏ (luật lệ, tập tục)
example_sentence: The newly ratified constitutional amendment sought to abolish feudal land tenure and redistribute arable acreage among peasant farmers.

en_meaning: Vile, detestable, or very unpleasant
vi_meaning: Đáng ghê tởm, tồi tệ kinh khủng
example_sentence: Frederick Douglass delivered searing orations detailing the abominable cruelties inherent in the institution of chattel slavery.

en_meaning: To soak up or take in information, liquids, or energy
vi_meaning: Hấp thụ, tiếp thu, thẩm thấu
example_sentence: Vast oceanic carbon sinks absorb roughly a quarter of all anthropogenic emissions, yet this uptake comes at the cost of accelerating acidification.

en_meaning: To restrain oneself from doing or enjoying something
vi_meaning: Kiêng nhịn, bỏ phiếu trắng
example_sentence: Adhering to a strict code of judicial impartiality, the supreme court justice chose to abstain from deliberations involving her former law firm.

en_meaning: Not self-indulgent, especially when eating and drinking
vi_meaning: Tiết chế, điều độ, đạm bạc
example_sentence: Despite reigning over one of Europe's wealthiest empires, the monarch maintained an abstemious regimen of simple fare and early morning physical drills.

en_meaning: The practice of restraining oneself from indulging in something
vi_meaning: Sự kiêng khem, sự tiết chế
example_sentence: Early public health advocates argued that voluntary abstinence from distilled spirits would drastically diminish poverty and urban crime rates.

en_meaning: Existing in thought or as an idea but not having a physical existence
vi_meaning: Trừu tượng, mang tính lý thuyết
example_sentence: Theoretical physicists often manipulate abstract mathematical constructs in multidimensional space years before experimentalists find empirical verification.

en_meaning: Difficult to understand; obscure or profound
vi_meaning: Khó hiểu, uyên thâm, thâm thúy
example_sentence: Wittgenstein’s early treatise presents an abstruse logical framework that confounded even his closest colleagues at Cambridge.

en_meaning: Existing or available in large quantities; plentiful
vi_meaning: Dồi dào, phong phú
example_sentence: Glacial runoff throughout the spring months guaranteed an abundant freshwater supply for the terraced agriculture of the Andean highlands.

en_meaning: Extremely offensive and insulting; using physical or verbal violence
vi_meaning: Lăng mạ, sỉ nhục, ngược đãi
example_sentence: Investigative journalists exposed the abusive working conditions within the sweatshops, where underage laborers endured twelve-hour shifts without ventilation.

en_meaning: To be next to or have a common boundary with something
vi_meaning: Tiếp giáp với, nằm sát cạnh
example_sentence: In colonial New England towns, private farmlands were mapped to directly abut the town common, ensuring equitable grazing access for all settlers.

en_meaning: Extremely bad; appalling or wretched
vi_meaning: Cực kỳ tồi tệ, thê thảm
example_sentence: The expedition was doomed by abysmal logistics, as inadequate provisions and faulty navigational charts left the crew stranded in the polar ice.

en_meaning: A very deep or seemingly bottomless chasm or void
vi_meaning: Vực thẳm, khoảng trống vô tận
example_sentence: Torn between diplomatic compromise and total war, the prime minister warned that another misstep would plunge the continent into an abyss of mutual destruction.

en_meaning: Relating to schools, education, and study; or purely theoretical
vi_meaning: Mang tính học thuật, lý thuyết
example_sentence: Since the opposing general had already signed an unconditional surrender, any retrospective debate over strategic maneuvers was rendered purely academic.

en_meaning: To agree to a demand, request, or treaty
vi_meaning: Đồng ý, nhượng bộ, chấp thuận
example_sentence: Surrounded by advancing allied forces and facing civilian insurrection, the beleaguered regent had no choice but to accede to the armistice terms.

en_meaning: To increase in speed or cause to happen more quickly
vi_meaning: Thúc đẩy, làm tăng tốc độ
example_sentence: The invention of the steam locomotive served to accelerate the economic integration of frontier territories into global trade networks.

en_meaning: To make more noticeable or prominent
vi_meaning: Làm nổi bật, nhấn mạnh
example_sentence: The stark contrast between the whitewashed colonnades and the deep crimson portico served to accentuate the dramatic proportions of the neoclassical facade.

en_meaning: Easy to approach, reach, enter, or understand
vi_meaning: Dễ tiếp cận, dễ hiểu
example_sentence: By replacing arcane Latin terminology with clear vernacular prose, the pioneering physician made preventative medicine accessible to rural practitioners.

en_meaning: A supplemental component that improves or adds to something else
vi_meaning: Phụ kiện, người tòng phạm
example_sentence: Under maritime criminal statutes, any merchant who knowingly provisions an illegal blockade runner can be prosecuted as an accessory to treason.

en_meaning: To praise enthusiastically and publicly
vi_meaning: Hoan nghênh, ca ngợi nồng nhiệt
example_sentence: Literary critics across the globe acclaimed her evocative memoir for illuminating the harrowing realities of political exile with unflinching honesty.

en_meaning: To adapt to a new climate, environment, or situation
vi_meaning: Thích nghi với môi trường mới
example_sentence: Biologists noted that high-altitude species develop enlarged lung capacities to help them acclimate to the hypobaric pressures of the alpine zone.

en_meaning: An upward slope, such as on a hill
vi_meaning: Dốc ngược, con dốc hướng lên
example_sentence: The weary pack mules struggled to haul heavy supply wagons up the steep acclivity leading to the mountain pass.

en_meaning: An expression of praise, approval, or a special distinction or award
vi_meaning: Giải thưởng danh giá, sự tán dương
example_sentence: Although the mathematician shunned public attention, her groundbreaking proof of the topology conjecture earned her the highest accolade in the field.

en_meaning: To provide lodging or space; to adjust or adapt to someone's needs
vi_meaning: Điều chỉnh để đáp ứng, cung cấp chỗ ở
example_sentence: The urban transit authority redesigned underground platforms to accommodate the dramatic surge in daily commuter volume projected for the coming decade.

en_meaning: A person who helps another commit a crime or do something wrong
vi_meaning: Kẻ đồng lõa, tòng phạm
example_sentence: During the treason trial, prosecutors demonstrated that the telegraph operator had acted as a willing accomplice by relaying encrypted military codes to enemy agents.

en_meaning: An official agreement or treaty; to give or grant someone power or status
vi_meaning: Hiệp định, sự đồng thuận
example_sentence: After months of contentious negotiations in Geneva, the rival factions signed a bilateral accord that mandated a phased withdrawal of heavy artillery.

en_meaning: To approach and address someone boldly or aggressively
vi_meaning: Tiếp cận và bắt chuyện đường đột, sấn tới
example_sentence: As the governor departed the statehouse, an agitated assembly of disenfranchised factory workers moved to accost him regarding unpaid wages.

en_meaning: To clothe or equip in something noticeable or impressive
vi_meaning: Trang bị đồ dùng, mặc quân phục ấn tượng
example_sentence: Quartermasters were ordered to accoutre every infantry battalion with reinforced wool greatcoats and cold-weather provisions prior to the alpine campaign.

en_meaning: The process of growth or increase by the gradual accumulation of additional layers or matter
vi_meaning: Sự bồi tụ dần dần, sự tích tụ thêm lớp
example_sentence: A barrier reef expands over millennia through the continuous accretion of calcium carbonate secreted by colonies of microscopic coral polyps.

en_meaning: To accumulate or receive payments or benefits over time
vi_meaning: Tích lũy dồn lại, sinh sôi theo thời gian
example_sentence: Substantial environmental dividends will accrue to municipalities that convert municipal bus fleets from fossil fuels to electric power.

en_meaning: Sharpness and directness in speech; sourness or bitterness in taste
vi_meaning: Sự chua chát, gay gắt (trong lời nói)
example_sentence: The literary critic was notorious for the relentless acerbity of her reviews, which frequently reduced aspiring novelists to tears.

en_meaning: Relating to or containing acetic acid; vinegary
vi_meaning: Có vị chua của giấm, thuộc về axit axetic
example_sentence: Prolonged exposure to oxygen spoils vintage wine by encouraging acetobacter proliferation, resulting in a sharp, acetic flavor reminiscent of vinegar.

en_meaning: Sharp-tasted or sour; somewhat acidic; caustic in style
vi_meaning: Hơi chua, châm biếm sâu cay
example_sentence: Beneath her polished aristocratic demeanor lay an acidulous wit that subtly undermined the self-importance of the royal court.

en_meaning: To accept or admit the existence or truth of something
vi_meaning: Thừa nhận, công nhận
example_sentence: Even the staunch defenders of laissez-faire capitalism had to acknowledge that unchecked monopolies ultimately stifle market innovation.

en_meaning: The highest point or stage; the peak of perfection
vi_meaning: Đỉnh cao, tột đỉnh, thời hoàng kim
example_sentence: Architects often cite the Parthenon as the acme of Classical Doric design, exemplifying harmonious proportions and subtle optical refinements.

en_meaning: The properties or qualities of a room that determine how sound is transmitted
vi_meaning: Độ vang âm, đặc tính âm học
example_sentence: Sound engineers retrofitted the amphitheater with convex acoustic baffles to optimize the hall's acoustics for symphonic performances.
